<h3>2.3 Google Calendar integration</h3>
<p>HOBS Companion offers mental health professionals on our platform the option to connect their own Google Calendar to the App.</p>
<p><strong>What we access.</strong> If a professional chooses to connect their calendar, we request permission to view and create calendar events on that professional's own Google Calendar. We do not access any other Google service (Gmail, Drive, Contacts, etc.), and we only ever access the calendar belonging to the professional who explicitly connects it — never a client's calendar, and never any calendar the professional hasn't personally authorized.</p>
<p><strong>Why we access it.</strong> This connection is used solely to:</p>
<ul>
  <li>Automatically create a calendar event (with a Google Meet video link) when a client books a session with that professional.</li>
  <li>Update or remove that event if the session is rescheduled or cancelled within HOBS Companion.</li>
  <li>Reflect changes made directly in Google Calendar back into HOBS Companion, so both stay in sync.</li>
  <li>Recognize when a professional has personal time blocked on their calendar, so that time is not offered to clients as available for booking.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>What we store.</strong> We store the OAuth access and refresh tokens needed to maintain this connection, encrypted at rest, along with the Google account email associated with the connection. We do not store the content of any calendar event that isn't related to a HOBS Companion session — for example, we do not read or retain details of a professional's personal appointments beyond knowing that a time slot is unavailable.</p>
<p><strong>How a professional can revoke access.</strong> A professional can disconnect their Google Calendar at any time from within the App (Profile/Schedule → Calendar → Disconnect), which immediately deletes the stored tokens. They can also revoke access directly from their Google Account's security settings at any time, independent of the App.</p>
<p><strong>Data sharing.</strong> We do not sell, rent, or share Google Calendar data with any third party. It is used exclusively for the scheduling functionality described above.</p>

<h2>3. Where your data is stored</h2>
<p>Your data is stored securely with Supabase, our database and backend provider, on cloud infrastructure located in Japan. Push notifications and usage analytics are processed through Google Firebase, which operates on Google's global infrastructure.</p>
<p>Access to your data within our systems is restricted using row-level security — in plain terms, our database is configured so that, by default, each person can only read their own data, and only designated admin or therapist accounts (for clients under their active care) can see more, and only what's relevant to that care relationship.</p>

OLD (exact):

document.getElementById('moodTrackerBackBtn').onclick = function(){ showOnly('panel-bubbles'); setActiveNav('navHome'); };

```

NEW (exact):
```
document.getElementById('moodTrackerBackBtn').onclick = function(){ showOnly('panel-bubbles'); setActiveNav('navHome'); };

// ================= PERIOD TRACKER =================
// Deliberately the most locked-down data in the app -- RLS on period_logs allows ONLY the
// owning user to read or write their own rows, full stop, not even admins or therapists (see
// "Users manage their own period logs" policy). Never touched by analytics beyond a generic
// screen-view (see logFirstPartyAnalytics elsewhere -- that already never logs content, just
// that the screen was opened), never synced anywhere else.
var periodDateModalMode = null; // 'start' | 'end'
var periodOngoingLogId = null;

document.getElementById('openPeriodTrackerBtn').onclick = function(){
  showOnly('panel-period-tracker');
  renderPeriodTracker();
};
document.getElementById('periodTrackerBackBtn').onclick = function(){ showOnly('panel-bubbles'); setActiveNav('navHome'); };

function formatPeriodDate(dateStr){
  return new Date(dateStr + 'T00:00:00').toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'short', year:'numeric' });
}
function daysBetween(a, b){
  return Math.round((new Date(b + 'T00:00:00') - new Date(a + 'T00:00:00')) / (1000*60*60*24));
}

function renderPeriodTracker(){
  sb.from('period_logs').select('*').eq('user_id', currentUser.id).order('start_date', {ascending:false}).then(function(result){
    var logs = (result.data || []);
    var activeCard = document.getElementById('periodActiveCard');
    var logStartBtn = document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn');
    var ongoing = logs.find(function(l){ return !l.end_date; });

    if(ongoing){
      periodOngoingLogId = ongoing.id;
      activeCard.style.display = 'block';
      document.getElementById('periodActiveSince').textContent = 'Started ' + formatPeriodDate(ongoing.start_date);
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'none';
    } else {
      periodOngoingLogId = null;
      activeCard.style.display = 'none';
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'block';
    }

    // Prediction: average the gap between the last few cycle START dates (up to 6), predict
    // forward from the most recent start. Needs at least 2 logged cycles to say anything --
    // never guesses off a single data point.
    var predictionCard = document.getElementById('periodPredictionCard');
    var notEnoughMsg = document.getElementById('periodNotEnoughDataMsg');
    var starts = logs.map(function(l){ return l.start_date; }).sort(); // oldest first
    if(starts.length >= 2){
      var recentStarts = starts.slice(-6);
      var gaps = [];
      for(var i = 1; i < recentStarts.length; i++) gaps.push(daysBetween(recentStarts[i-1], recentStarts[i]));
      var avgCycle = Math.round(gaps.reduce(function(sum, g){ return sum + g; }, 0) / gaps.length);
      var lastStart = recentStarts[recentStarts.length - 1];
      var predictedDate = new Date(lastStart + 'T00:00:00');
      predictedDate.setDate(predictedDate.getDate() + avgCycle);
      predictionCard.style.display = 'block';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionDate').textContent = predictedDate.toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'long' });
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionMeta').textContent = 'Based on your last ' + recentStarts.length + ' cycles — average ' + avgCycle + ' days';
    } else {
      predictionCard.style.display = 'none';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'block';
    }

    var historyEl = document.getElementById('periodHistoryList');
    if(logs.length === 0){
      historyEl.innerHTML = '<p style="font-size:12px;color:#9AABCE;text-align:center;">Nothing logged yet — tap "Log Period Start" whenever it begins.</p>';
      return;
    }
    historyEl.innerHTML = logs.map(function(l){
      var lengthLabel = l.end_date ? (daysBetween(l.start_date, l.end_date) + 1) + ' days' : 'Ongoing';
      var rangeLabel = formatPeriodDate(l.start_date) + (l.end_date ? ' – ' + formatPeriodDate(l.end_date) : '');
      return '<div style="background:#FFFFFF;border:1px solid #EEE0C4;border-radius:14px;padding:12px 14px;margin-bottom:8px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;">'+
        '<p style="font-size:12.5px;font-weight:700;color:#2A2013;margin:0;">'+rangeLabel+'</p>'+
        '<p style="font-size:11px;color:#C2588A;font-weight:700;margin:0;">'+lengthLabel+'</p>'+
      '</div>';
    }).join('');
  });
}

document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn').onclick = function(){
  periodDateModalMode = 'start';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalTitle').textContent = 'Log Period Start';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').style.display = 'block';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModal').style.display = 'block';
};
document.getElementById('periodLogEndBtn').onclick = function(){
  periodDateModalMode = 'end';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalTitle').textContent = 'Log Period End';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').style.display = 'block';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModal').style.display = 'block';
};
function closePeriodDateModal(){
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModal').style.display = 'none';
}
document.getElementById('periodDateModalCancelBtn').onclick = closePeriodDateModal;
document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').onclick = closePeriodDateModal;
document.getElementById('periodDateModalSaveBtn').onclick = function(){
  var dateVal = document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value;

function showOnly(panelId){
  var previousPanel = panelHistoryStack[panelHistoryStack.length - 1];
  allPanels.forEach(function(id){ document.getElementById(id).style.display = (id === panelId) ? 'block' : 'none'; });
  // panel-chat-room needs flex (not the generic block above) for its own internal header/
  // messages/input column layout to actually work as intended.
  if(panelId === 'panel-chat-room') document.getElementById('panel-chat-room').style.display = 'flex';
  // Real ask: this button should only ever be visible on the Journal index page itself, not
  // floating over every single screen in the app the way it originally did.
  document.getElementById('newJournalEntryFabBtn').style.display = (panelId === 'panel-history') ? 'flex' : 'none';
  // Screenshot/screen-recording prevention in chats: @capacitor/privacy-screen was already a
  // real dependency (confirmed in package.json) but never actually called anywhere -- the
  // plugin requires an explicit enable()/disable() call, it does nothing just by being
  // installed. Hooked here rather than only on one exit button specifically because the
  // plugin's own docs warn to toggle on every navigation, including back navigation -- this
  // way it's correct regardless of HOW someone leaves a chat room (back button, tapping a nav
  // tab, a notification tap that jumps elsewhere, etc.), not just one specific path.
  if(IS_NATIVE_APP && window.Capacitor && window.Capacitor.Plugins && window.Capacitor.Plugins.PrivacyScreen){
    if(panelId === 'panel-chat-room' && previousPanel !== 'panel-chat-room'){
      window.Capacitor.Plugins.PrivacyScreen.enable({ android: { dimBackground: true } }).catch(function(){});
    } else if(panelId !== 'panel-chat-room' && previousPanel === 'panel-chat-room'){
      window.Capacitor.Plugins.PrivacyScreen.disable().catch(function(){});
    }
  }
  if(panelHistoryStack[panelHistoryStack.length - 1] !== panelId){
    var fromPanel = panelHistoryStack[panelHistoryStack.length - 1];
    panelHistoryStack.push(panelId);
    if(panelHistoryStack.length > 30) panelHistoryStack.shift(); // avoid unbounded growth
    logScreenView(panelId, fromPanel);
  }
  var shownPanel = document.getElementById(panelId);
  if(shownPanel) setTimeout(function(){ shownPanel.querySelectorAll('textarea').forEach(autoGrowTextarea); }, 0);
}

document.getElementById('periodTrackerBackBtn').onclick = function(){ showOnly('panel-bubbles'); setActiveNav('navHome'); };

function formatPeriodDate(dateStr){
  return new Date(dateStr + 'T00:00:00').toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'short', year:'numeric' });
}
function daysBetween(a, b){
  return Math.round((new Date(b + 'T00:00:00') - new Date(a + 'T00:00:00')) / (1000*60*60*24));
}

function renderPeriodTracker(){
  sb.from('period_logs').select('*').eq('user_id', currentUser.id).order('start_date', {ascending:false}).then(function(result){
    var logs = (result.data || []);
    var activeCard = document.getElementById('periodActiveCard');
    var logStartBtn = document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn');
    var ongoing = logs.find(function(l){ return !l.end_date; });

    if(ongoing){
      periodOngoingLogId = ongoing.id;
      activeCard.style.display = 'block';
      document.getElementById('periodActiveSince').textContent = 'Started ' + formatPeriodDate(ongoing.start_date);
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'none';
    } else {
      periodOngoingLogId = null;
      activeCard.style.display = 'none';
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'block';
    }

    // Prediction: average the gap between the last few cycle START dates (up to 6), predict
    // forward from the most recent start. Needs at least 2 logged cycles to say anything --
    // never guesses off a single data point.
    var predictionCard = document.getElementById('periodPredictionCard');
    var notEnoughMsg = document.getElementById('periodNotEnoughDataMsg');
    var starts = logs.map(function(l){ return l.start_date; }).sort(); // oldest first
    if(starts.length >= 2){
      var recentStarts = starts.slice(-6);
      var gaps = [];
      for(var i = 1; i < recentStarts.length; i++) gaps.push(daysBetween(recentStarts[i-1], recentStarts[i]));
      var avgCycle = Math.round(gaps.reduce(function(sum, g){ return sum + g; }, 0) / gaps.length);
      var lastStart = recentStarts[recentStarts.length - 1];
      var predictedDate = new Date(lastStart + 'T00:00:00');
      predictedDate.setDate(predictedDate.getDate() + avgCycle);
      predictionCard.style.display = 'block';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionDate').textContent = predictedDate.toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'long' });
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionMeta').textContent = 'Based on your last ' + recentStarts.length + ' cycles — average ' + avgCycle + ' days';
    } else {
      predictionCard.style.display = 'none';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'block';
    }

    var historyEl = document.getElementById('periodHistoryList');
    if(logs.length === 0){
      historyEl.innerHTML = '<p style="font-size:12px;color:#9AABCE;text-align:center;">Nothing logged yet — tap "Log Period Start" whenever it begins.</p>';
      return;
    }
    historyEl.innerHTML = logs.map(function(l){
      var lengthLabel = l.end_date ? (daysBetween(l.start_date, l.end_date) + 1) + ' days' : 'Ongoing';
      var rangeLabel = formatPeriodDate(l.start_date) + (l.end_date ? ' – ' + formatPeriodDate(l.end_date) : '');
      return '<div style="background:#FFFFFF;border:1px solid #EEE0C4;border-radius:14px;padding:12px 14px;margin-bottom:8px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:center;">'+
        '<p style="font-size:12.5px;font-weight:700;color:#2A2013;margin:0;">'+rangeLabel+'</p>'+
        '<p style="font-size:11px;color:#C2588A;font-weight:700;margin:0;">'+lengthLabel+'</p>'+
      '</div>';
    }).join('');
  });
}

document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn').onclick = function(){
  periodDateModalMode = 'start';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalTitle').textContent = 'Log Period Start';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value = new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);

document.getElementById('periodTrackerBackBtn').onclick = function(){ showOnly('panel-bubbles'); setActiveNav('navHome'); };

function formatPeriodDate(dateStr){
  return new Date(dateStr + 'T00:00:00').toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'short', year:'numeric' });
}
function daysBetween(a, b){
  return Math.round((new Date(b + 'T00:00:00') - new Date(a + 'T00:00:00')) / (1000*60*60*24));
}

function renderPeriodChips(containerId, options, selectedRef, multiSelect){
  var container = document.getElementById(containerId);
  container.innerHTML = options.map(function(opt){
    var isSelected = multiSelect ? selectedRef.indexOf(opt) !== -1 : selectedRef === opt;
    return '<button type="button" class="period-chip" data-val="'+opt+'" style="padding:8px 13px;border-radius:20px;border:1.5px solid '+(isSelected?'#C2588A':'#EEE0C4')+';background:'+(isSelected?'#C2588A':'transparent')+';color:'+(isSelected?'#FFFFFF':'#5C6B94')+';font-size:12px;font-weight:600;cursor:pointer;">'+opt+'</button>';
  }).join('');
  container.querySelectorAll('.period-chip').forEach(function(chip){
    chip.onclick = function(){
      var val = chip.dataset.val;
      if(multiSelect){
        var idx = selectedRef.indexOf(val);
        if(idx === -1) selectedRef.push(val); else selectedRef.splice(idx, 1);
      } else {
        if(containerId === 'periodFlowChips') periodSelectedFlow = (periodSelectedFlow === val) ? null : val;
      }
      renderPeriodChips(containerId, options, containerId === 'periodFlowChips' ? periodSelectedFlow : selectedRef, multiSelect);
    };
  });
}

function renderPeriodTracker(){
  sb.from('period_logs').select('*').eq('user_id', currentUser.id).order('start_date', {ascending:false}).then(function(result){
    var logs = (result.data || []);
    var activeCard = document.getElementById('periodActiveCard');
    var logStartBtn = document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn');
    var ongoing = logs.find(function(l){ return !l.end_date; });

    if(ongoing){
      periodOngoingLogId = ongoing.id;
      activeCard.style.display = 'block';
      document.getElementById('periodActiveSince').textContent = 'Started ' + formatPeriodDate(ongoing.start_date);
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'none';
    } else {
      periodOngoingLogId = null;
      activeCard.style.display = 'none';
      logStartBtn.style.display = 'block';
    }

    // Prediction: average the gap between the last few cycle START dates (up to 6), predict
    // forward from the most recent start. Needs at least 2 logged cycles to say anything --
    // never guesses off a single data point.
    var predictionCard = document.getElementById('periodPredictionCard');
    var notEnoughMsg = document.getElementById('periodNotEnoughDataMsg');
    var starts = logs.map(function(l){ return l.start_date; }).sort(); // oldest first
    if(starts.length >= 2){
      var recentStarts = starts.slice(-6);
      var gaps = [];
      for(var i = 1; i < recentStarts.length; i++) gaps.push(daysBetween(recentStarts[i-1], recentStarts[i]));
      var avgCycle = Math.round(gaps.reduce(function(sum, g){ return sum + g; }, 0) / gaps.length);
      var lastStart = recentStarts[recentStarts.length - 1];
      var predictedDate = new Date(lastStart + 'T00:00:00');
      predictedDate.setDate(predictedDate.getDate() + avgCycle);
      predictionCard.style.display = 'block';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'none';
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionDate').textContent = predictedDate.toLocaleDateString('en-IN', { day:'numeric', month:'long' });
      document.getElementById('periodPredictionMeta').textContent = 'Based on your last ' + recentStarts.length + ' cycles — average ' + avgCycle + ' days';
    } else {
      predictionCard.style.display = 'none';
      notEnoughMsg.style.display = 'block';
    }

    var historyEl = document.getElementById('periodHistoryList');
    if(logs.length === 0){
      historyEl.innerHTML = '<p style="font-size:12px;color:#9AABCE;text-align:center;">Nothing logged yet — tap "Log Period Start" whenever it begins.</p>';
      return;
    }
    historyEl.innerHTML = logs.map(function(l){
      var lengthLabel = l.end_date ? (daysBetween(l.start_date, l.end_date) + 1) + ' days' : 'Ongoing';
      var rangeLabel = formatPeriodDate(l.start_date) + (l.end_date ? ' – ' + formatPeriodDate(l.end_date) : '');
      var tags = [];
      if(l.flow_intensity) tags.push(l.flow_intensity);
      (l.physical_symptoms || []).forEach(function(s){ tags.push(s); });
      (l.mood_symptoms || []).forEach(function(s){ tags.push(s); });
      var tagsHtml = tags.length ? '<p style="font-size:10.5px;color:#B0708F;margin:4px 0 0;">'+tags.join(' · ')+'</p>' : '';
      return '<div style="background:#FFFFFF;border:1px solid #EEE0C4;border-radius:14px;padding:12px 14px;margin-bottom:8px;">'+
        '<div style="display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;">'+
          '<div><p style="font-size:12.5px;font-weight:700;color:#2A2013;margin:0;">'+rangeLabel+'</p>'+tagsHtml+'</div>'+
          '<p style="font-size:11px;color:#C2588A;font-weight:700;margin:0;white-space:nowrap;">'+lengthLabel+'</p>'+
        '</div>'+
        '<div style="display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:10px;">'+
          '<button class="period-edit-btn" data-id="'+l.id+'" style="flex:1;padding:8px;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #EEE0C4;background:transparent;color:#5C6B94;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">Edit</button>'+
          '<button class="period-delete-btn" data-id="'+l.id+'" style="flex:1;padding:8px;border-radius:10px;border:1px solid #F0C7C7;background:transparent;color:#C77B7B;font-size:11px;font-weight:700;cursor:pointer;">Delete</button>'+
        '</div>'+
      '</div>';
    }).join('');

    historyEl.querySelectorAll('.period-edit-btn').forEach(function(btn){
      btn.onclick = function(){
        var log = logs.find(function(l){ return l.id === btn.dataset.id; });
        openPeriodModal('edit', log);
      };
    });
    historyEl.querySelectorAll('.period-delete-btn').forEach(function(btn){
      btn.onclick = function(){
        if(!confirm('Delete this logged cycle? This cannot be undone.')) return;
        sb.from('period_logs').delete().eq('id', btn.dataset.id).then(function(result){
          if(result.error){ showToast('Could not delete — please try again.'); return; }
          showToast('Removed.');
          renderPeriodTracker();
        });
      };
    });
  });
}

function openPeriodModal(mode, existingLog){
  periodDateModalMode = mode;
  periodEditingLogId = existingLog ? existingLog.id : null;
  periodSelectedFlow = existingLog ? (existingLog.flow_intensity || null) : null;
  periodSelectedPhysical = existingLog ? (existingLog.physical_symptoms || []).slice() : [];
  periodSelectedMood = existingLog ? (existingLog.mood_symptoms || []).slice() : [];

  var symptomFieldsShown = (mode === 'start' || mode === 'edit');
  document.getElementById('periodSymptomFields').style.display = symptomFieldsShown ? 'block' : 'none';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalTitle').textContent = mode === 'end' ? 'Log Period End' : (mode === 'edit' ? 'Edit Cycle' : 'Log Period Start');
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value = existingLog ? existingLog.start_date : new Date().toISOString().slice(0, 10);
  document.getElementById('periodNotesInput').value = existingLog ? (existingLog.notes || '') : '';

  if(symptomFieldsShown){
    renderPeriodChips('periodFlowChips', PERIOD_FLOW_OPTIONS, periodSelectedFlow, false);
    renderPeriodChips('periodPhysicalChips', PERIOD_PHYSICAL_OPTIONS, periodSelectedPhysical, true);
    renderPeriodChips('periodMoodChips', PERIOD_MOOD_OPTIONS, periodSelectedMood, true);
  }
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').style.display = 'block';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModal').style.display = 'block';
}

document.getElementById('periodLogStartBtn').onclick = function(){ openPeriodModal('start', null); };
document.getElementById('periodLogEndBtn').onclick = function(){ openPeriodModal('end', null); };

function closePeriodDateModal(){
  document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('periodDateModal').style.display = 'none';
}
document.getElementById('periodDateModalCancelBtn').onclick = closePeriodDateModal;
document.getElementById('periodDateModalBackdrop').onclick = closePeriodDateModal;
document.getElementById('periodDateModalSaveBtn').onclick = function(){
  var dateVal = document.getElementById('periodDateModalInput').value;
  if(!dateVal){ showToast('Pick a date first.'); return; }
  var btn = this;
  btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Saving...';

  if(periodDateModalMode === 'end'){
    sb.from('period_logs').update({ end_date: dateVal }).eq('id', periodOngoingLogId).then(function(result){
      btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Save';
      if(result.error){ showToast('Could not save — please try again.'); return; }
      closePeriodDateModal();
      renderPeriodTracker();
    });
    return;
  }

  var payload = {
    flow_intensity: periodSelectedFlow,
    physical_symptoms: periodSelectedPhysical,
    mood_symptoms: periodSelectedMood,
    notes: document.getElementById('periodNotesInput').value.trim() || null
  };

  if(periodDateModalMode === 'start'){
    payload.user_id = currentUser.id;
    payload.start_date = dateVal;
    sb.from('period_logs').insert(payload).then(function(result){
      btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Save';
      if(result.error){ showToast('Could not save — please try again.'); return; }
      logAnalyticsEvent('period_logged');
      closePeriodDateModal();
      renderPeriodTracker();
    });
  } else { // edit
    payload.start_date = dateVal;
    sb.from('period_logs').update(payload).eq('id', periodEditingLogId).then(function(result){
      btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Save';
      if(result.error){ showToast('Could not save — please try again.'); return; }
      closePeriodDateModal();
      renderPeriodTracker();
    });
  }
};

    // no explicit setTheme() call, Android falls back to the <application>-level default theme
    // (@style/AppTheme, which extends Theme.AppCompat.Light.DarkActionBar), so a real native

    // very first line of onCreate(), before super.onCreate() runs.
    @Override
    public void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {

        WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(getWindow(), false);

## ⚠️ MANDATORY DEPLOY PROCESS

Every web deploy MUST update BOTH to the same new value:
1. `version.json` at the repo root — `{"build": "<value>"}`
2. `CURRENT_BUILD` variable near the top of `index.html`'s main `<script>` block
Recommended value: `date -u +%Y%m%d%H%M%S`

**Real mistake made this session, worth remembering**: forgot to `git add version.json` alongside `index.html` in one commit — the live site served the new code correctly but reported the OLD build number, since `version.json` never actually got pushed. Caught by checking the raw committed file rather than assuming a clean push. Always verify both files are actually staged before committing, not just index.html.

Any NEW Edge Function must avoid the `@supabase/supabase-js` SDK import and use raw `fetch()` — this project's deploy pipeline can't resolve remote esm.sh imports.

**UTF-8/base64 encoding gotcha** (found this session, real production bug caused by it): plain `atob()`/`btoa()` are NOT UTF-8 safe for any Edge Function reading/writing text via GitHub's Contents API. Use `new TextDecoder('utf-8').decode(Uint8Array.from(atob(b64), c => c.charCodeAt(0)))` to decode, and a proper chunked bytes-to-base64 helper to encode — see `update-donate-page-meta/index.ts` for the working implementation. This was done from a completely empty sandbox this session. Full steps that actually worked, including two real gotchas:

2. **GOTCHA #1 — only a JRE is pre-installed, not a full JDK.** `java -version` works but `javac` does not exist, and Gradle will fail with a cryptic "Toolchain installation ... does not provide the required capabilities: [JAVA_COMPILER]" error. Fix: `apt-get install -y openjdk-21-jdk-headless`.

3. Set up the project: `npm install` (from this package's `code/package.json`), then `npx cap add android` (scaffolds a fresh Capacitor Android project from template — this is fine and expected even though it's not literally the same folder as any prior session's, since we're overlaying our own customized files on top anyway).

4. **Overlay the customized native files** on top of the freshly-scaffolded project (paths relative to the scaffolded `android/` folder):
   - `code/AndroidManifest.xml` → `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
   - `android-native/build.gradle` → `android/app/build.gradle`
   - `android-native/top-level-build.gradle` → `android/build.gradle`
   - `android-native/variables.gradle` → `android/variables.gradle`
   - `android-native/styles.xml` → `android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml`
   - `android-native/MainActivity.java` → `android/app/src/main/java/com/hobsfoundation/companion/MainActivity.java`
   - `keystore/hobs-release.keystore` → `android/hobs-release.keystore`
   - `keystore/google-services.json` → `android/app/google-services.json`
   Then `npx cap sync android` to pull in fresh web assets + register native plugins. Confirmed this does NOT clobber the custom native files above — sync only touches web assets and plugin registration.

5. **GOTCHA #2 — background builds die when the shell session ends.** A plain `nohup ... &` is not enough; the sandbox appears to kill child processes when the invoking shell tears down between tool calls. Use `setsid nohup ./gradlew assembleRelease --no-daemon > build.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &` instead — `setsid` fully detaches it from the session. The build itself took under 2 minutes once dependencies were cached.

## SESSION UPDATE — A REAL NATIVE BUG FOUND, ONLY VISIBLE ON AN ACTUAL DEVICE

Akash reported a stray white title bar showing a truncated app name ("HOBS_Co...") sitting above the app's actual content on a real device. This was **never once visible during any web-based testing this entire project** — a browser cannot render a native Android action bar at all, so this bug was invisible to every Playwright test run across every prior session.

**Root cause, confirmed via direct file inspection**: `MainActivity`'s manifest entry uses `AppTheme.NoActionBarLaunch` only for the splash sequence. Standard Capacitor practice is for `MainActivity.onCreate()` to call `setTheme(R.style.AppTheme_NoActionBar)` as its very first line, switching away from the launch theme once splash is done. **This call was never present in this codebase, in any prior session.** Without it, Android falls back to the `<application>`-level default theme (`@style/AppTheme`, which extends `Theme.AppCompat.Light.DarkActionBar`) — producing exactly the reported bar.

**Fixed** by adding the missing `setTheme()` call. **Verified at the compiled-bytecode level** (not just source review) via `dexdump` — the literal first two instructions inside the compiled `onCreate()` are: load the `AppTheme_NoActionBar` resource ID, then call `setTheme()` with it, before anything else runs including `super.onCreate()`. As close to certain as static analysis gets without a physical device.

Shipped in v2.7 (versionCode 18) — see build recipe above. **Genuinely not yet confirmed on a real device** as of this doc's writing.

## SESSION UPDATE — SCREENSHOT PREVENTION IN CHATS, NOW ACTUALLY WIRED (WAS INERT BEFORE)

`@capacitor/privacy-screen` was a real declared dependency in `package.json` this entire time, but **nothing in the app's JS ever called it.** This specific plugin requires an explicit `PrivacyScreen.enable()`/`.disable()` call — it does nothing whatsoever just from being installed.

Fixed by hooking into the central `showOnly()` navigation function: `enable()` fires the moment someone enters `panel-chat-room`, `disable()` fires the moment they leave it, regardless of exit path (back button, nav tap, notification jump) — matching the plugin's own documented guidance to toggle on every navigation, not just one exit button.

**Confirmed the plugin's real native code — including actual `Window.addFlags()` calls, the real mechanism `FLAG_SECURE` uses — is compiled into the v2.7 APK** via bytecode disassembly of `PrivacyScreenDialog`. Not yet confirmed to actually block a real screenshot attempt on a physical device.

## SESSION UPDATE — PERIOD TRACKER, BUILT FROM NOTHING

New feature, requested and built this session. Real, clinically-grounded field choices rather than guessed — researched ACOG's "menstrual cycle as a vital sign" guidance and the standard field sets used by real apps (Flo, Clue) before building, per direct request.

**Schema**: `period_logs` (see schema reference above). **RLS is the strictest pattern in the whole app** — owner-only, full stop, not even admins or therapists get an exception. This was a deliberate design choice given how sensitive this data is.

**What it actually asks**: flow intensity (Spotting/Light/Medium/Heavy), physical symptoms (Cramps, Headache, Bloating, Back pain, Breast tenderness, Fatigue, Nausea, Acne), and — deliberately, since this is specifically relevant to HOBS's own mission — a dedicated mood/mental-health symptom set (Irritability, Anxiety, Low mood, Mood swings, Brain fog), since PMDD/PMS-to-mood correlation is squarely inside what this app is for. Deliberately did NOT build full fertility-awareness tracking (basal temperature, cervical mucus) — that's a different app's job. Every field is optional; nothing is forced before someone can just log that their period started.

**Prediction**: averages the gap between the last up-to-6 logged cycle start dates, predicts forward from the most recent one. Requires at least 2 logged cycles — never guesses off a single data point.

**Edit and delete** on every history entry, added per direct request. Edit reopens the same form fully pre-filled (including all previously-selected symptom chips); delete asks for confirmation first.

Fully tested live end-to-end, including editing a value and confirming the change persisted, and deleting and confirming actual removal. Test data cleaned up after each round.

Accessible from a new "Period Tracker" card on Home's quick-access grid.

FULL FILE TEXT (exact):
```
// delete-user-account
//
// Two ways to call this:
//   1. Self-service: { "selfDelete": true } -- any signed-in user can delete their OWN account
//      and all their own data. This is the new path, added to satisfy Google Play's account
//      deletion requirement (an in-app path is required, not just an admin-triggered one).
//      Blocked for staff accounts (is_admin or is_therapist) -- deleting a professional's
//      account has real knock-on effects for their actual clients (active bookings, chat
//      history, calendar connections) that deserve a human looking at it first, not a silent
//      self-service button. Staff members needing to leave get a clear message to contact
//      support instead.
//   2. Admin-triggered: { "userId": "<target>" } -- unchanged from before, still requires the
//      caller to be an admin, still blocks an admin from targeting their own account through
//      this path (use selfDelete for that instead).
//
// Fully deletes a user's account: all their data across every table that references them, and
// their actual login (auth.users row) via the Supabase Auth Admin API, which requires the
// service role key and cannot be done from client-side JS with just RLS permissions -- RLS
// doesn't govern auth.users itself, regardless of how permissive public-schema policies are.
//
// REAL GAP FOUND AND FIXED THIS REWRITE: the previous version's table list (notification_
// recipients, subtasks, tasks, entries, expert_bookings, test_results, worksheet_responses,
// donations) predates a lot of what's been built since -- chat, support groups, the period
// tracker, WHO-5, consent agreements, credits, and more. Confirmed directly against a live
// schema query for every table with a user-referencing column before rewriting this, rather
// than trusting the old list was still complete.
//
// Two categories of handling, not just one flat delete list:
//   HARD DELETE  -- entirely personal data, safe to remove outright.
//   SOFT-TOUCH   -- shared/referenced-by-others data, where a hard delete would break things
//                   for OTHER people (a group chat's history, a donation's financial record).
//                   Anonymized/soft-deleted instead of removed.
//
// Request body: { "selfDelete": true } OR { "userId": string }
// Response: { "success": true } or { "error": string }

import { createClient } from "https://esm.sh/@supabase/supabase-js@2";

const SUPABASE_URL = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_URL");
const SUPABASE_ANON_KEY = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_ANON_KEY");
const SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = Deno.env.get("SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY");

const corsHeaders = {
  "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*",
  "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "authorization, x-client-info, apikey, content-type",
  "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "POST, OPTIONS",
};

function jsonResponse(body: unknown, status: number) {
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
    status,
    headers: { ...corsHeaders, "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  });
}

// Entirely personal -- every row belonging to this user, in this table, is simply gone.
const HARD_DELETE_TABLES = [
  "notification_recipients",
  "subtasks",
  "tasks",
  "entries",
  "expert_bookings",
  "test_results",
  "worksheet_responses",
  "who5_entries",
  "period_logs",
  "consent_agreements",
  "credit_log",
  "chat_poll_votes",
  "chat_room_members",
  "app_analytics_events",
  "error_logs",
  "app_update_reminders",
  "gcal_connect_state_tokens",
  "professional_calendar_connections",
];

async function deleteAllDataFor(adminClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient>, userId: string) {
  for (const table of HARD_DELETE_TABLES) {
    await adminClient.from(table).delete().eq("user_id", userId);
  }

  // SOFT-TOUCH: chat messages -- hard-deleting these would leave real gaps in other people's
  // conversation history (a support group mid-discussion, a coordination thread). The app
  // already has a "deleted" flag it actively respects in rendering (shows "Message deleted"),
  // so use that existing, already-supported path instead of a destructive delete.
  await adminClient.from("chat_messages").update({ deleted: true, text: null }).eq("sender_id", userId);

  // SOFT-TOUCH: donations -- a financial/accounting record, plausibly needed for 80G tax
  // receipt and bookkeeping purposes independent of the donor's account existing. Strip the
  // identifying fields, keep the transaction record itself (amount, date, campaign, confirmed
  // status) intact.
  await adminClient.from("donations").update({ user_id: null, donor_name: null }).eq("user_id", userId);

  await adminClient.from("profiles").delete().eq("user_id", userId);
}

Deno.serve(async (req) => {
  if (req.method === "OPTIONS") return new Response("ok", { headers: corsHeaders });

  try {
    const authHeader = req.headers.get("Authorization") || "";
    if (!authHeader) return jsonResponse({ error: "Missing Authorization header" }, 401);

    const callerClient = createClient(SUPABASE_URL!, SUPABASE_ANON_KEY!, {
      global: { headers: { Authorization: authHeader } },
    });
    const { data: callerAuth, error: callerAuthErr } = await callerClient.auth.getUser();
    if (callerAuthErr || !callerAuth?.user) return jsonResponse({ error: "Invalid or expired session" }, 401);

    const adminClient = createClient(SUPABASE_URL!, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY!);
    const body = await req.json().catch(() => ({}));

    let targetUserId: string;

    if (body.selfDelete === true) {
      const { data: callerProfile } = await adminClient
        .from("profiles")
        .select("is_admin, is_therapist")
        .eq("user_id", callerAuth.user.id)
        .single();
      if (callerProfile?.is_admin || callerProfile?.is_therapist) {
        return jsonResponse(
          { error: "Staff accounts can't be self-deleted here since it affects your clients too -- please contact us directly and we'll help." },
          400
        );
      }
      targetUserId = callerAuth.user.id;
    } else {
      const { userId } = body;
      if (!userId || typeof userId !== "string") return jsonResponse({ error: "userId is required" }, 400);

      const { data: callerProfile } = await adminClient
        .from("profiles")
        .select("is_admin")
        .eq("user_id", callerAuth.user.id)
        .single();
      if (!callerProfile?.is_admin) return jsonResponse({ error: "Admin access required" }, 403);
      if (userId === callerAuth.user.id) {
        return jsonResponse({ error: "Use selfDelete to delete your own account through this tool" }, 400);
      }
      targetUserId = userId;
    }

    await deleteAllDataFor(adminClient, targetUserId);

    const { error: authDeleteErr } = await adminClient.auth.admin.deleteUser(targetUserId);
    if (authDeleteErr) {
      return jsonResponse({ error: "Data deleted, but removing the login failed: " + authDeleteErr.message }, 500);
    }

    return jsonResponse({ success: true }, 200);
  } catch (err) {
    return jsonResponse({ error: String(err) }, 500);
  }
});

```

// ================= SELF-SERVICE ACCOUNT DELETION =================
// Real gap found and fixed: delete-user-account previously existed but was admin-triggered
// only, and explicitly BLOCKED a user from targeting their own account through it at all.
// Google Play's account deletion policy expects a genuine in-app self-service path, not just
// an admin action -- this is that path. Staff accounts (is_admin/is_therapist) are still
// blocked here, same as server-side, since deleting a professional's account has real
// knock-on effects for their actual clients that deserve a person looking at it, not a solo
// button tap -- shown as a clear message up front rather than letting them type DELETE first
// and only then finding out.
document.getElementById('epDeleteAccountBtn').onclick = function(){
  if(appState.isAdmin || appState.isTherapist){
    showToast("Staff accounts can't be deleted here since it affects your clients too — please message us directly and we'll help.");
    return;
  }
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountConfirmInput').value = '';
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountError').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountModalBackdrop').style.display = 'block';
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountModal').style.display = 'block';
};
function closeDeleteAccountModal(){
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountModalBackdrop').style.display = 'none';
  document.getElementById('deleteAccountModal').style.display = 'none';
}
document.getElementById('deleteAccountCancelBtn').onclick = closeDeleteAccountModal;
document.getElementById('deleteAccountModalBackdrop').onclick = closeDeleteAccountModal;
document.getElementById('deleteAccountConfirmBtn').onclick = function(){
  var typed = document.getElementById('deleteAccountConfirmInput').value.trim().toUpperCase();
  var errorEl = document.getElementById('deleteAccountError');
  if(typed !== 'DELETE'){
    errorEl.textContent = 'Type DELETE exactly to confirm.';
    errorEl.style.display = 'block';
    return;
  }
  var btn = this;
  btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Deleting...';
  sb.functions.invoke('delete-user-account', { body: { selfDelete: true } }).then(function(result){
    btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Permanently Delete';
    var errored = result.error || (result.data && result.data.error);
    if(errored){
      errorEl.textContent = (result.data && result.data.error) || 'Something went wrong — please try again, or message us directly.';
      errorEl.style.display = 'block';
      return;
    }
    closeDeleteAccountModal();
    showToast("Your account has been deleted. We're sorry to see you go.");
    document.getElementById('logoutBtn').click();
  }).catch(function(){
    btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Permanently Delete';
    errorEl.textContent = 'Something went wrong — please try again, or message us directly.';
    errorEl.style.display = 'block';
  });
};

// Entirely personal -- every row belonging to this user, in this table, is simply gone.
const HARD_DELETE_TABLES = [
  "notification_recipients",
  "subtasks",
  "tasks",
  "entries",
  "expert_bookings",
  "test_results",
  "worksheet_responses",
  "who5_entries",
  "period_logs",
  "consent_agreements",
  "credit_log",
  "chat_poll_votes",
  "chat_room_members",
  "app_analytics_events",
  "error_logs",
  "app_update_reminders",
  "gcal_connect_state_tokens",
  "professional_calendar_connections",
];

async function deleteAllDataFor(adminClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient>, userId: string) {
  for (const table of HARD_DELETE_TABLES) {
    await adminClient.from(table).delete().eq("user_id", userId);
  }

  // SOFT-TOUCH: chat messages -- hard-deleting these would leave real gaps in other people's
  // conversation history (a support group mid-discussion, a coordination thread). The app
  // already has a "deleted" flag it actively respects in rendering (shows "Message deleted"),
  // so use that existing, already-supported path instead of a destructive delete.
  await adminClient.from("chat_messages").update({ deleted: true, text: null }).eq("sender_id", userId);

  // SOFT-TOUCH: donations -- a financial/accounting record, plausibly needed for 80G tax
  // receipt and bookkeeping purposes independent of the donor's account existing. Strip the
  // identifying fields, keep the transaction record itself (amount, date, campaign, confirmed
  // status) intact.
  await adminClient.from("donations").update({ user_id: null, donor_name: null }).eq("user_id", userId);

  await adminClient.from("profiles").delete().eq("user_id", userId);
}

// Entirely personal -- every row belonging to this user, in this table, is simply gone.

// removed outright rather than anonymized; a professional's own calendar/schedule data has no

const PROFESSIONAL_HARD_DELETE_TABLES = [
  "calendar_change_requests",
  "session_calendar_events",
  "professional_busy_blocks",
];

async function deleteAllDataFor(adminClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient>, userId: string) {

    await adminClient.from(table).delete().eq("user_id", userId);
  }
  for (const table of PROFESSIONAL_HARD_DELETE_TABLES) {

```
async function deleteStorageFolder(adminClient: ReturnType<typeof createClient>, bucket: string, prefix: string) {
  // REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED via a live test with an actual uploaded file: Storage's .list()
  // is NOT recursive -- it only returns direct children of the given prefix. A file uploaded to
  // {userId}/profile-photos/photo.png was being completely missed, because .list(userId) only
  // saw "profile-photos" as an opaque folder entry, never descended into it, and so never found
  // the actual file to delete. Confirmed the file was still present after "deletion" before this
  // fix. A folder entry has id === null; a real file entry always has a real id. Walk the whole
  // tree before batch-removing every actual file path collected.
  const allFilePaths: string[] = [];
  async function walk(currentPrefix: string) {
    const { data: entries } = await adminClient.storage.from(bucket).list(currentPrefix, { limit: 1000 });
    if (!entries) return;
    for (const entry of entries) {
      const entryPath = `${currentPrefix}/${entry.name}`;
      if (entry.id === null) {
        await walk(entryPath); // it's a subfolder -- descend
      } else {
        allFilePaths.push(entryPath); // it's a real file
      }
    }
  }
  await walk(prefix);
  if (allFilePaths.length > 0) {
    await adminClient.storage.from(bucket).remove(allFilePaths);
  }
}
```

function showWelcomeBackScreen(){
  var overlay = document.getElementById('welcomeBackOverlay');
  var img = document.getElementById('welcomeBackImg');
  // Real bug found and fixed: this used to be a static src on the img tag, which browsers
  // start downloading the moment the HTML parses -- regardless of the containing div being
  // display:none. That meant every single user, on every single load, was downloading this
  // image even if they'd never actually see it (first-time users, or before auth even
  // resolves), adding real weight to the initial page load. Setting src here instead, only at
  // the moment this screen is actually about to be shown, means it's never fetched for anyone
  // who doesn't reach this exact point.
  if(!img.src) img.src = 'bob-welcome-back.jpg';
  overlay.style.display = 'block';
  overlay.onclick = function(){
    overlay.style.display = 'none';
    overlay.onclick = null;
    showOnly('panel-bubbles');
    renderHomeGreeting();
  };
}
```

NEW (exact):
```
function showWelcomeBackScreen(){
  var overlay = document.getElementById('welcomeBackOverlay');
  var leafLeft = document.getElementById('welcomeBackLeafLeft');
  var leafRight = document.getElementById('welcomeBackLeafRight');
  var seam = document.getElementById('welcomeBackSeam');
  // Real bug found and fixed in an earlier session, still preserved here: a static src/
  // background-image loads the moment the HTML parses, regardless of the containing div being
  // display:none. Setting it here instead, only at the moment this screen is actually about to
  // be shown, means it's never fetched for anyone who doesn't reach this exact point.
  if(!leafLeft.style.backgroundImage){
    leafLeft.style.backgroundImage = "url('bob-welcome-back.jpg')";
    leafRight.style.backgroundImage = "url('bob-welcome-back.jpg')";
  }
  overlay.style.display = 'block';
  // Restart the open animation cleanly every time this screen shows (not just the first) --
  // removing the class, forcing a reflow, then re-adding it is the standard way to make a CSS
  // animation replay instead of silently no-op-ing because the class never actually changed.
  [leafLeft, leafRight, seam].forEach(function(el){ el.classList.remove('opening'); });
  void overlay.offsetWidth;
  [leafLeft, leafRight, seam].forEach(function(el){ el.classList.add('opening'); });
  overlay.onclick = function(){
    overlay.style.display = 'none';
    overlay.onclick = null;
    showOnly('panel-bubbles');
    renderHomeGreeting();
  };
}
```

  // Real bug found and fixed in an earlier session, still preserved here: a static src/

  // animation replay instead of silently no-op-ing because the class never actually changed.
  [leafLeft, leafRight, seam].forEach(function(el){ el.classList.remove('opening'); });
  void overlay.offsetWidth;

var WELCOME_PAGE_SLICE_COUNT = 14;
function buildWelcomeBackSlices(){

  if(container.childElementCount === WELCOME_PAGE_SLICE_COUNT) return; // already built once, reuse
  container.innerHTML = '';
  var n = WELCOME_PAGE_SLICE_COUNT;

    slice.className = 'wb-slice';
    var widthPct = 100 / n;
    slice.style.left = (i * widthPct) + '%';
    slice.style.width = widthPct + '%';
    slice.style.backgroundImage = "url('bob-welcome-back.jpg')";

// Shown to genuinely returning users only -- anyone who's already completed onboarding, signed
// the basic ToS, cleared the consent gate if it applied, and seen the first-time walkthrough.
// First-time flow (showOnboarding, showWalkthrough) is completely untouched by this.
function showWelcomeBackScreen(){
  var overlay = document.getElementById('welcomeBackOverlay');
  var shadeEl = document.getElementById('welcomeBackShade');
  buildWelcomeBackSlices();
  overlay.style.display = 'block';

  var reducedMotion = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;
  var slices = document.querySelectorAll('#welcomeBackPageTurn .wb-slice');
  var n = slices.length;
  slices.forEach(function(slice, i){
    slice.getAnimations().forEach(function(anim){ anim.cancel(); }); // let it replay cleanly every showing, not just once
    if(reducedMotion){
      slice.style.transform = 'rotateY(0deg)';
      return;
    }
    // The actual "page turn with curve" mechanic: every slice shares the same left-edge hinge,
    // but the slice nearest the hinge starts barely turned while the slice at the free (right)
    // edge starts turned almost all the way over -- that fan of different starting angles is
    // what makes the page visibly bend/curl as it turns, instead of the whole thing rotating
    // together as one rigid flat plane (which is what a flat rotateY on a single element would
    // look like, and isn't a real page turn).
    var startAngle = -88 * (i / (n - 1));
    slice.style.transform = 'rotateY(' + startAngle + 'deg)';
    slice.animate(
      [ { transform: 'rotateY(' + startAngle + 'deg)' }, { transform: 'rotateY(0deg)' } ],
      { duration: 800, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.3,.9,.4,1)', delay: i * 6, fill: 'forwards' }
    );
  });
  shadeEl.classList.remove('opening');
  void shadeEl.offsetWidth;
  if(!reducedMotion) shadeEl.classList.add('opening');

  overlay.onclick = function(){
    overlay.style.display = 'none';
    overlay.onclick = null;
    showOnly('panel-bubbles');
    renderHomeGreeting();
  };
}

    )

        page.on("pageerror", lambda exc: errors.append(str(exc)))

        for attempt in range(6):
            dismissed_any = False
            for sel in ["#walkthroughFinishBtn", "#consentGateSubmitBtn", "#authOverlay"]:
                el = await page.query_selector(sel)
                if el and await el.is_visible():
                    try:
                        await el.click(timeout=2000)
                        dismissed_any = True
                        await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
            if not dismissed_any:
                break

        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        overlay_visible = await page.is_visible("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        print("\nOverlay visible:", overlay_visible)
        slice_count_after = await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('welcomeBackPageTurn').childElementCount")
        print("Slices built (should be 14):", slice_count_after)

        # Check mid-animation: read actual computed transforms of first, middle, last slice
        await page.wait_for_timeout(120)
        mid_state = await page.evaluate("""
            () => {
                const slices = document.querySelectorAll('#welcomeBackPageTurn .wb-slice');
                const first = getComputedStyle(slices[0]).transform;
                const mid = getComputedStyle(slices[Math.floor(slices.length/2)]).transform;
                const last = getComputedStyle(slices[slices.length-1]).transform;
                return {first, mid, last};
            }
        """)
        print("\nMid-animation transforms (should be DIFFERENT from each other -- that's the curve):")
        print("First slice (near hinge):", mid_state['first'])
        print("Middle slice:", mid_state['mid'])
        print("Last slice (free edge):", mid_state['last'])
        await page.screenshot(path="/tmp/pageturn_mid.png")

        # Wait for full settle
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1200)
        settled_state = await page.evaluate("""
            () => {
                const slices = document.querySelectorAll('#welcomeBackPageTurn .wb-slice');
                return Array.from(slices).map(s => getComputedStyle(s).transform);
            }
        """)
        all_identity = all(t == 'matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)' or t == 'none' for t in settled_state)
        print("\nAll slices settled to flat/identity:", all_identity)
        await page.screenshot(path="/tmp/pageturn_settled.png")

        # Tap to dismiss, trigger again (simulate returning a second time) to confirm replay works
        await page.click("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(500)

        print("\nErrors:", errors)
        await browser.close()
    server.terminate()

asyncio.run(main())

```
// Shown to genuinely returning users only -- anyone who's already completed onboarding, signed
// the basic ToS, cleared the consent gate if it applied, and seen the first-time walkthrough.
// First-time flow (showOnboarding, showWalkthrough) is completely untouched by this.
var WB_FLAT_CLIP = 'polygon(100% 0%, 0% 0%, 0% 25%, 0% 50%, 0% 75%, 0% 100%, 100% 100%)';
var WB_CURLED_CLIP = 'polygon(100% 0%, 9% 0%, 7% 25%, 13% 50%, 7% 75%, 9% 100%, 100% 100%)';
function showWelcomeBackScreen(){
  var overlay = document.getElementById('welcomeBackOverlay');
  var pageEl = document.getElementById('welcomeBackPage');
  var shadeEl = document.getElementById('welcomeBackShade');
  // Real bug found and fixed in an earlier session, still preserved here: a static background-
  // image loads the moment the HTML parses, regardless of the containing div being display:none.
  // Setting it here instead, only at the moment this screen is actually about to be shown, means
  // it's never fetched for anyone who doesn't reach this exact point.
  if(!pageEl.style.backgroundImage) pageEl.style.backgroundImage = "url('bob-welcome-back.jpg')";
  overlay.style.display = 'block';

  pageEl.getAnimations().forEach(function(anim){ anim.cancel(); }); // let it replay cleanly every showing, not just once
  shadeEl.getAnimations().forEach(function(anim){ anim.cancel(); });
  var reducedMotion = window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches;

  // Arrives already folded shut against the right-side hinge -- no auto-play. A tap is what
  // starts the turn now, per direct request, rather than it playing the instant this screen
  // appears.
  pageEl.style.clipPath = WB_FLAT_CLIP;
  if(reducedMotion){
    pageEl.style.transform = 'rotateY(0deg)';
    shadeEl.style.opacity = '0';
  } else {
    pageEl.style.transform = 'rotateY(85deg)';
    shadeEl.style.background = 'linear-gradient(90deg, rgba(0,0,0,0.45) 0%, rgba(0,0,0,0) 65%)';
    shadeEl.style.opacity = '0';
  }

  var playing = false;
  overlay.onclick = function(){
    if(reducedMotion){
      overlay.style.display = 'none';
      overlay.onclick = null;
      showOnly('panel-bubbles');
      renderHomeGreeting();
      return;
    }
    if(playing) return; // ignore extra taps mid-turn
    playing = true;
    // Slow and smooth, closer to the weight of the existing book-cover-open animation (1.3s)
    // than the quicker in-app page flips, since this is a bigger once-per-session moment, not
    // something that repeats constantly. The clip-path keyframes are what add the actual curve
    // -- the free (left) edge bows inward mid-turn, then straightens back out flat -- composed
    // together with the rotation itself, rather than a flat rectangle just tilting in place.
    var pageAnim = pageEl.animate(
      [
        { transform: 'rotateY(85deg)',  clipPath: WB_FLAT_CLIP,   offset: 0 },
        { transform: 'rotateY(38deg)',  clipPath: WB_CURLED_CLIP, offset: 0.55 },
        { transform: 'rotateY(0deg)',   clipPath: WB_FLAT_CLIP,   offset: 1 }
      ],
      { duration: 1500, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.5,.02,.4,1)', fill: 'forwards' }
    );
    shadeEl.animate(
      [ { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 0.55, offset: 0.5 }, { opacity: 0 } ],
      { duration: 1500, easing: 'ease-out', fill: 'forwards' }
    );
    var finish = function(){
      overlay.style.display = 'none';
      overlay.onclick = null;
      showOnly('panel-bubbles');
      renderHomeGreeting();
    };
    if(pageAnim.finished && pageAnim.finished.then) pageAnim.finished.then(finish).catch(finish);
    else setTimeout(finish, 1550);
  };
}
```

                    try:
                        await el.click(timeout=2000)
                        dismissed_any = True
                        await page.wait_for_timeout(800)
                    except Exception:
                        pass
            if not dismissed_any:
                break

        await page.wait_for_timeout(300)
        overlay_visible = await page.is_visible("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        print("Overlay visible:", overlay_visible)

        # Check it arrives FOLDED, not flat, and stays that way without a tap
        initial_transform = await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('welcomeBackPage').style.transform")
        print("Initial (pre-tap) inline transform (should be rotateY(85deg)):", initial_transform)

        await page.wait_for_timeout(1000)  # wait a while -- should NOT auto-play
        still_visible = await page.is_visible("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        still_folded = await page.evaluate("getComputedStyle(document.getElementById('welcomeBackPage')).transform")
        print("Still visible after 1s with no tap:", still_visible)
        print("Still folded (not identity) after 1s with no tap:", still_folded != 'matrix(1, 0, 0, 1, 0, 0)')

        # Now tap it
        await page.click("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        await page.wait_for_timeout(50)

        anim_config = await page.evaluate("""
            () => {
                const el = document.getElementById('welcomeBackPage');
                const anim = el.getAnimations()[0];
                if (!anim) return null;
                return { keyframes: anim.effect.getKeyframes(), timing: anim.effect.getTiming() };
            }
        """)
        print("\nAnimation config after tap:")
        print("Keyframes:", anim_config['keyframes'] if anim_config else None)
        print("Timing:", anim_config['timing'] if anim_config else None)

        # Tap again immediately -- should be ignored (still same animation, not restarted)
        await page.click("#welcomeBackOverlay", force=True)
        await page.wait_for_timeout(50)
        anim_count_after_double_tap = await page.evaluate("document.getElementById('welcomeBackPage').getAnimations().length")
        print("\nAnimation count after double-tap (should still be 1, not 2):", anim_count_after_double_tap)

        # Wait for it to fully finish and navigate away
        await page.wait_for_timeout(1700)
        overlay_visible_after = await page.is_visible("#welcomeBackOverlay")
        home_visible = await page.is_visible("#panel-bubbles")
        print("\nOverlay visible after animation completes (should be False):", overlay_visible_after)
        print("Home panel visible after animation completes (should be True):", home_visible)

        print("\nErrors:", errors)
        await browser.close()
    server.terminate()

asyncio.run(main())

    shadeEl.style.opacity = '0';
  }

  var playing = false;
  overlay.onclick = function(){
    if(reducedMotion){
      overlay.style.display = 'none';
      overlay.onclick = null;
      showOnly('panel-bubbles');
      renderHomeGreeting();
      return;
    }
    if(playing) return; // ignore extra taps mid-turn
    playing = true;
    // Slow and smooth, closer to the weight of the existing book-cover-open animation (1.3s)
    // than the quicker in-app page flips, since this is a bigger once-per-session moment, not
    // something that repeats constantly. The clip-path keyframes are what add the actual curve
    // -- the free (left) edge bows inward mid-turn, then straightens back out flat -- composed
    // together with the rotation itself, rather than a flat rectangle just tilting in place.
    var pageAnim = pageEl.animate(
      [
        { transform: 'rotateY(-32deg)', clipPath: WB_FLAT_CLIP,   offset: 0 },
        { transform: 'rotateY(-26deg)', clipPath: WB_CURLED_CLIP, offset: 0.18 },
        { transform: 'rotateY(-18deg)', clipPath: WB_FLAT_CLIP,   offset: 0.35 },
        { transform: 'rotateY(0deg)',   clipPath: WB_FLAT_CLIP,   offset: 1 }
      ],
      { duration: 1500, easing: 'cubic-bezier(.5,.02,.4,1)', fill: 'forwards' }
    );
    shadeEl.animate(
      [ { opacity: 0 }, { opacity: 0.55, offset: 0.18 }, { opacity: 0, offset: 0.4 } ],
      { duration: 1500, easing: 'ease-out', fill: 'forwards' }
    );
    var finish = function(){
      overlay.style.display = 'none';
      overlay.onclick = null;
      showOnly('panel-bubbles');
      renderHomeGreeting();
    };
    if(pageAnim.finished && pageAnim.finished.then) pageAnim.finished.then(finish).catch(finish);
    else setTimeout(finish, 1550);
  };
}
```

  // Real bug found and fixed in an earlier session: this used to be a static src on the img
  // tag, which browsers start downloading the moment the HTML parses -- regardless of the

  // is actually about to be shown, means it's never fetched for anyone who doesn't reach this

  overlay.onclick = function(){

  };
}

```
function renderDayPanel(){
  var parts = activeDayKey.split('-').map(Number);
  var dObj = new Date(parts[0], parts[1]-1, parts[2]);
  document.getElementById('dayDateTitle').textContent = dObj.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { weekday:'long', month:'long', day:'numeric' });
  document.getElementById('dayHeaderLabel').textContent = (activeDayKey === TODAY_KEY) ? 'Today' : dObj.toLocaleDateString('en-US', { weekday:'long' });
  renderDayProgressStrip();
  var moodArea = document.getElementById('dayMoodArea');
  var dayMoods = moodsForDate(activeDayKey);
  if(dayMoods.length){
    moodArea.innerHTML = '<div class="mood-chip-row">' + dayMoods.map(function(m){
      return '<span class="mood-chip-cal" style="background:'+m.color+'22;"><span class="mood-dot-cal" style="width:8px;height:8px;background:'+m.color+';display:inline-block;"></span>'+m.label+'</span>';
    }).join('') + '</div>';
  } else {
    moodArea.innerHTML = '<p class="empty-mood">No mood logged this day yet.</p>';
  }
  document.getElementById('startBodyDoubleBtn').style.display = (activeDayKey === TODAY_KEY) ? 'block' : 'none';
  renderTaskListCal();
}
// A task with subtasks counts as fractionally done based on its own subtasks (matching the same
// "derive from real subtask state, never trust task.done blindly" rule already used in
// renderTaskListCal just below), not as one flat unit -- a 3-subtask task with 1 done
// contributes 1/3 of a "task" toward the strip, not 0.
function renderDayProgressStrip(){
  var strip = document.getElementById('dayProgressStrip');
  var label = document.getElementById('dayProgressLabel');
  var tasks = getTasks(activeDayKey);
  if(tasks.length === 0){
    strip.innerHTML = '';
    label.textContent = 'Nothing on the list yet for this day.';
    return;
  }
  var totalUnits = 0, doneUnits = 0;
  tasks.forEach(function(task){
    if(task.subtasks && task.subtasks.length > 0){
      totalUnits += task.subtasks.length;
      doneUnits += task.subtasks.filter(function(s){ return s.done; }).length;
    } else {
      totalUnits += 1;
      doneUnits += task.done ? 1 : 0;
    }
  });
  var segments = tasks.length; // one segment per task, filled proportionally to how much of the strip's overall progress it represents
  var pctDone = totalUnits > 0 ? (doneUnits / totalUnits) : 0;
  var filledSegments = Math.round(pctDone * segments);
  strip.innerHTML = '';
  for(var i = 0; i < segments; i++){
    var dot = document.createElement('div');
    dot.style.cssText = 'flex:1;height:6px;border-radius:3px;background:'+(i < filledSegments ? '#3B8F63' : '#EEE0C4')+';transition:background 0.4s ease;';
    strip.appendChild(dot);
  }
  var doneTasks = tasks.filter(function(t){ return t.subtasks && t.subtasks.length > 0 ? t.subtasks.every(function(s){ return s.done; }) : t.done; }).length;
  label.textContent = doneTasks === tasks.length ? 'Everything done for this day.' : (doneTasks + ' of ' + tasks.length + ' tasks done');
}
```

asyncio.run(main())

// A task with subtasks counts as fractionally done based on its own subtasks (matching the same
// "derive from real subtask state, never trust task.done blindly" rule already used in
// renderTaskListCal just below), not as one flat unit -- a 3-subtask task with 1 done
// contributes 1/3 of a "task" toward the strip, not 0.
function renderDayProgressStrip(){
  var strip = document.getElementById('dayProgressStrip');
  var label = document.getElementById('dayProgressLabel');
  var tasks = getTasks(activeDayKey);

    strip.innerHTML = '';
    label.textContent = 'Nothing on the list yet for this day.';
    return;
  }

  tasks.forEach(function(task){
    if(task.subtasks && task.subtasks.length > 0){
      totalUnits += task.subtasks.length;

    // WebView draw behind both bars and actually show through that reclaimed space, giving the
    // app the phone's real full screen. Real safe-area insets are correctly reported to the web

    // action bar was showing above the WebView on every actual device -- invisible to any
    // browser-based testing, since a browser can't render a native Android action bar at all.
    // This is the standard Capacitor pattern: switch to the real no-action-bar theme as the
    // very first line of onCreate(), before super.onCreate() runs.
    @Override

package com.hobsfoundation.companion;

import android.app.NotificationChannel;
import android.app.NotificationManager;
import android.graphics.Color;
import android.os.Build;
import android.os.Bundle;
import androidx.core.view.WindowCompat;
import androidx.webkit.WebSettingsCompat;
import androidx.webkit.WebViewFeature;
import com.getcapacitor.BridgeActivity;

public class MainActivity extends BridgeActivity {
    // Real, confirmed cause of colors coming out wrong (a leather-brown cover rendering as
    // teal/green) on devices with system-wide \"Force Dark\" enabled, common on MIUI/Xiaomi --
    // WebView's algorithmic darkening will recolor any page that hasn't explicitly opted out.
    // The page now declares color-scheme: light in both a meta tag and CSS, but that alone
    // isn't always honored consistently across every OEM's WebView build, so this explicitly
    // disables algorithmic darkening at the native level too, for the most reliable fix.
    //
    // Also: real root cause found and fixed for reported pillarboxing on the welcome-back
    // screen. This app was rendering in standard (non-edge-to-edge) mode -- the status bar and
    // navigation bar both reserved their own opaque space, shrinking the WebView's actual usable
    // viewport below the phone's true physical screen dimensions. Confirmed directly: a device
    // screenshot at exactly 720x1600 (9:20, matching the welcome-back image's own ratio
    // precisely) still showed gaps on the sides, because the *effective* viewport being rendered
    // into was shorter than that -- not a sizing mistake in the image itself, a real native
    // configuration gap. setDecorFitsSystemWindows(false) plus transparent system bars lets the
    // WebView draw behind both bars and actually show through that reclaimed space, giving the
    // app the phone's real full screen. Real safe-area insets are correctly reported to the web
    // layer via CSS env(safe-area-inset-*), which this app already uses in several places
    // (button placement near the bottom edge, etc.), so nothing else needs to change there.
    // REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED: this activity's manifest entry uses AppTheme.NoActionBarLaunch
    // only for the splash sequence -- but nothing ever switched the theme back afterward. With
    // no explicit setTheme() call, Android falls back to the <application>-level default theme
    // (@style/AppTheme, which extends Theme.AppCompat.Light.DarkActionBar), so a real native
    // action bar was showing above the WebView on every actual device -- invisible to any
    // browser-based testing, since a browser can't render a native Android action bar at all.
    // This is the standard Capacitor pattern: switch to the real no-action-bar theme as the
    // very first line of onCreate(), before super.onCreate() runs.
    //
    // REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED: scheduled/recurring push notifications (journal reminder, task
    // reminders, etc.) were reported as consistently not showing up, despite FCM itself
    // confirming successful delivery to the device every time -- while ad-hoc notifications
    // (a booking request, a support-group message) did get through and get opened. The
    // difference: this app never explicitly created its own notification channel, so Android
    // auto-created a fallback one the very first time a background notification ever arrived --
    // and critically, once a channel is auto-created, ITS IMPORTANCE LEVEL IS LOCKED for that
    // install; no later app update can raise it, only the person manually changing it in
    // Settings or a full uninstall/reinstall. If that very first background notification arrived
    // under conditions where Android defaulted the auto-created channel to low/silent importance,
    // every notification since would have been genuinely delivered but silent or invisible --
    // fully consistent with "FCM says delivered, I never see it" being unrelated to battery
    // settings. Explicitly creating a HIGH-importance channel here, and pointing FCM at it by ID
    // via the manifest meta-data below, ensures any fresh install gets it right from the very
    // first notification. This cannot retroactively fix an existing install's already-locked
    // channel -- that still needs the person to check Settings > Apps > HOBS Companion >
    // Notifications and raise the channel's importance manually, or reinstall.
    private void createNotificationChannel() {
        if (Build.VERSION.SDK_INT >= Build.VERSION_CODES.O) {
            NotificationChannel channel = new NotificationChannel(
                "hobs_default_channel",
                "HOBS Companion",
                NotificationManager.IMPORTANCE_HIGH
            );
            channel.setDescription("Reminders and messages from HOBS Companion");
            NotificationManager manager = getSystemService(NotificationManager.class);
            if (manager != null) {
                manager.createNotificationChannel(channel);
            }
        }
    }

    @Override
    public void onCreate(Bundle savedInstanceState) {
        setTheme(R.style.AppTheme_NoActionBar);
        WindowCompat.setDecorFitsSystemWindows(getWindow(), false);
        super.onCreate(savedInstanceState);
        createNotificationChannel();
        getWindow().setStatusBarColor(Color.TRANSPARENT);
        getWindow().setNavigationBarColor(Color.TRANSPARENT);
        if (getBridge() != null && getBridge().getWebView() != null
                && WebViewFeature.isFeatureSupported(WebViewFeature.ALGORITHMIC_DARKENING)) {
            WebSettingsCompat.setAlgorithmicDarkeningAllowed(getBridge().getWebView().getSettings(), false);
        }
    }

// person, not a fixed server timezone), app version (so the update-nudge job knows who's
// behind), and device model/OS version (so a real notification-delivery issue like a channel
// importance problem can actually be traced to a specific phone brand, instead of guessing).
// The device info comes straight from the WebView's own user agent string -- Android reliably
// includes the real device model there (e.g. "Android 13; SM-G991B"), so this needs no new
// native plugin or APK rebuild, unlike app_version_code/name above. Runs quietly on every
// sign-in.
function parseDeviceInfoFromUserAgent(ua){
  var result = { osVersion: null, deviceModel: null };
  if(!ua) return result;
  var androidMatch = ua.match(/Android\s+([\d.]+);\s*([^)]+)\)/);
  if(androidMatch){
    result.osVersion = 'Android ' + androidMatch[1];
    // The device-model segment sometimes has "Build/XXXXX" trailing on the same clause --
    // strip that off, it's a firmware build id, not part of the model name.
    result.deviceModel = androidMatch[2].replace(/\s*Build\/.*/i, '').trim();
  }
  return result;
}

FULL FILE TEXT (exact):
````
# HOBS Companion App Icon — Persistent Assets

## Why this folder exists
The native Android build environment is fully ephemeral — every session that builds a new APK
starts from `npx cap add android`, which scaffolds a completely fresh Android project and
regenerates Capacitor's *default* icon. Custom native files (MainActivity.java, AndroidManifest.xml,
etc.) get overlaid back on top from documented sources each time, but the app icon was never on
that list until now — so every rebuild was silently reverting to the generic default icon, even
though it had been correctly set in an earlier session. This folder is the fix: a permanent,
version-controlled copy of the real icon, so any future session can restore it in one step.

## How to reapply these in a fresh build
After `npx cap add android` and before running the build, copy these files into place:

```
cp android-native-assets/icons/mipmap-mdpi/*.png    android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-mdpi/
cp android-native-assets/icons/mipmap-hdpi/*.png    android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-hdpi/
cp android-native-assets/icons/mipmap-xhdpi/*.png   android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-xhdpi/
cp android-native-assets/icons/mipmap-xxhdpi/*.png  android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-xxhdpi/
cp android-native-assets/icons/mipmap-xxxhdpi/*.png android/app/src/main/res/mipmap-xxxhdpi/
cp android-native-assets/icons/ic_launcher_background.xml android/app/src/main/res/values/
```

This should be added to the same "overlay these custom files after scaffolding" step used for
MainActivity.java, AndroidManifest.xml, styles.xml, variables.gradle, and the two build.gradle
files — treat it as one more required file in that list, not a separate one-off step.

## What's in each file
- `mipmap-{density}/ic_launcher.png` and `ic_launcher_round.png` — legacy pre-Android-8 icons,
  a plain square crop of Bob (the elephant mascot) at 48/72/96/144/192px.
- `mipmap-{density}/ic_launcher_foreground.png` — the adaptive-icon (Android 8+) foreground
  layer, 108/162/216/324/432px canvases with the same Bob crop scaled to 78% and centered with
  transparent padding, so the face stays inside the safe zone regardless of which mask shape
  (circle/squircle/rounded square) a given launcher applies.
- `ic_launcher_background.xml` — the adaptive-icon background color, `#82BCD9`, sampled directly
  from the sky in the source image rather than left as Capacitor's default white.
- `SOURCE_master_icon_crop.png` — the 780x780 square crop of the full character illustration
  this was all generated from. If the icon ever needs regenerating at different crop/zoom, start
  from this file (or from the full original character illustration if an even earlier stage is
  needed) rather than re-cropping from scratch.

## Verification, if redoing this in a new session
Don't just trust that the files copied — AAPT2 renames every resource to a short obfuscated
filename in a release build, so `find` won't locate `ic_launcher.png` by name inside a built APK.
Verify with `aapt dump badging` (shows the actual `application-icon` path) and
`aapt dump --values resources` (resolves that path's resource ID to its real packaged filename
and, for the background, its actual compiled color value) — cross-check the compiled background
color matches `#ff82bcd9` and that the foreground PNG's alpha channel has real transparent
padding (a solid full-bleed alpha channel would mean the old default snuck back in).

````

// sync-test-result-to-hubspot
//
// Sends a completed test result into HubSpot, matching the same real mechanism the website's
// own free screening form already uses (create/find a Contact by email, attach the result) --
// but as a Note on the contact rather than overwriting a single field, so a client's result
// history stays intact across multiple tests over time instead of each new one erasing the last.
// Scoring logic below is a direct, verified port of the app's own client-side scoring
// (bandInterpret + the per-dimension reverse-scoring sum, the Big Five percentage-based levels,
// and the PSQI's real 7-component clinical algorithm) -- extracted programmatically from the
// live app source rather than retyped by hand, and diffed against real client-side output for
// several tests before trusting it, specifically to avoid a subtly wrong recomputed score
// sitting in the CRM.
//
// REAL BUG FOUND AND FIXED: this function existed, fully built and correct, but was
// unreachable -- it only accepted a scheduler secret that the app's client-side code can never
// safely hold (embedding it in the app would expose it to anyone who decompiled the APK). That
// is the actual reason "hubspot" never appeared anywhere in the app's own source: there was
// never a safe way to call this. Fixed by adding a second, real path: a genuinely signed-in
